newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TIGER ONE STROKE BACK IN HUNT FOR THIRD SUCCESSIVE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TIGER ONE STROKE BACK IN HUNT FOR THIRD SUCCESSIVE TITLE.

text.p: David Ogrin used a string of six consecutive birdies to fire an eight-under-par 62 on Saturday, putting himself one shot ahead of Tiger Woods heading into the final round of the Colonial tournament.
Ogrin's round was two strokes better than his best round as a professional and one off the tournament single-round record as he vaulted into the lead.
But it seems likely that Ogrin, who stood at 15-under 195 for three rounds, will need another sensational performance to hold off the stalking Tiger.
Woods, who only got his first look at the course earlier this week, lowered his score for the third successive round, posting a six-under 64 as he moved in on his third consecutive PGA Tour victory.
Overnight co-leader Paul Goydos was alone in third at 197, two shots back of Ogrin after carding a 68.
Woods and Ogrin will be paired Sunday, but the 21-year-old sensation's Saturday playing partner, Fred Funk, seemed to think an air of inevitability was blowing Woods's way.
"That's the way it was when (Jack) Nicklaus was in his prime, he put fear in people," Funk said. "Tiger's the king now, he's taken over for Arnie."
Woods was pleased with Saturday's performance, which included seven birdies and one bogey.
"I'm getting all the parts clicking at the same time," Woods said. "I'm getting comfortable with the golf course and getting comfortable off the tee."

Woods birdied the first hole before bogeying the fourth to drop to even-par for the day. But that was his lone miscue as he added birdied at six and eight on the front side and birdied holes 11, 14, 15 and 17 for a back nine of 31.
"I just want to get myself into position for the final stretch on Sunday," said Woods, who finished his round with a par-saving eight-foot putt.
"If other people are playing me, in a sense that helps me. They should be playing the course, at least until the final couple of holes."
Since the front nine in the first round of the Masters, where he shot 40, Woods is an astounding 53-under-par for his last 189 holes of competition.
Ogrin said he was eager for the final-round matchup with Woods.
"Who would you rather beat then Tiger Woods?" he asked.
When Ogrin claimed his only PGA Tour victory last October, Woods started the final round seven shots back, cut the deficit to two strokes, then fell short to Ogrin on the final two holes.
"I'm a charter member of the Tiger killing club," Ogrin joked. "There aren't many of us out there."

Ogrin started the day at seven under par and four shots out of the lead. He had his first birdie at the par-5 second hole, then reeled off six in a row -- one off the tournament record -- on holes 7-12.
Ogrin added one more birdie on the par-4 14th hole before parring the rest of the way.
"It was a good round for me," he said. "A very, very good round. I was able to get my putter going and I played with a lot of confidence."
